_about: Luke's no-phone rule (2026-11-06), the shared case list for both email gates: pioneerleads scripts/humanize_gate.py (tests/test_send_gate.py) and, on the Mac, brown-bison-gov data/phone_gate.py (report only: test_mac_phone_gate_parity_report). 'cell': Luke's number in a form a gate must refuse; 'not_cell': other numbers that must pass; 'refuse': call invites; 'pass': trade wording, third parties, photos, negations. Builder + review lists, 2026-11-06; review #3 (2026-11-06): callback promises, more invite shapes, split / spelled forms of the cell, and RFP 'the call' wording. Review #4 (2026-11-06 13:40 MT probe): first-person promises to call or ring the reader's side ('I'll give your office a call', 'Luke will call Jake'), plural calls / callbacks offered, bare cell / text / mobile offers, filler before talk / hop on, talk-soon times, Teams / Meet / sync-up invites, SMS / Signal / voice notes; phone as equipment (jack, cable, VoIP system, poles, the phone company), negations ('better than a call', 'can't talk on the phone') and locate / inspection calls must pass. Review #5 (CEO session 2026-11-06, Luke's rule that no operator promises Luke will phone anyone): a first-person subject (I / we / let me / Luke / he meaning Luke) promising to call, phone or give a call to ANY person or organisation is refused, third parties included ('I'll give the inspector a call', 'We'll call the Town for the gate code', 'I'll phone the County tomorrow'); calling 811, calling for / calling in an inspection or locate, imperatives to the reader ('Give the inspector a call before you pour'), third parties calling each other and naming ('I'd call that a fair price') pass.
